scope: 30 exact historical keys outside other assignments; original operators and endpoint scopes inspected. Full pages 402–403 and 412–413 re-read to distinguish economic incidence, military force and disease outcomes.

rows.review_disposition: 032D can internalize the Tribun du peuple and radical networks disseminating Babeuf’s class interpretation. Preserve the publication as an access route to ideas and organizing, without turning all hardship protest into adherence to his doctrine.

60C460 must preserve emancipation, war and military autonomy, but correct the old endpoint’s undifferentiated defeat of Spanish and British intervention. Full 412 attributes Spanish expulsion to black forces; 413 stresses disease and British withdrawal. Retain racial violence and fragile authority without attributing every outcome to battlefield victory.

C455 can internalize the Nîmes bagarre within southern Catholic royalism. Preserve early Catholic–Protestant antagonism and the episode’s date, rather than retroactively deriving it from the later oath schism.

60C460 can internalize militarization enabling Toussaint’s autonomy and durable resistance. Full 413 distinguishes autonomy while loyal to France, capture, renewed resistance after slavery restoration and eventual independence; do not make Toussaint personally lead every final stage.

DCF7/7593/C479 may internalize the manifesto within the 1792 intervention. Preserve émigré influence and political consequences; C389’s particular mechanism is not equivalent to every membership claim.

2AC must retain colonial struggle driving successive rights concessions, including the limited 1791 qualification and 1792 extension. Retire the unbound conflict label while preserving metropolitan inconsistency and pressure from events.

A4EB/2FE1/E37B must retain liberation language as justification for expansion alongside domination and extraction. Attribute the justification to revolutionary actors; do not endorse it as a sufficient explanation or excuse for coercion.
Reject the anachronistic cause: invasion planning in 1797–1798 did not initiate the war with Britain already underway since 1793. DA4B retains the attempt to end or redirect that continuing war.

3F2B can internalize discreet subsidies to selected Jacobin papers as tactical anti-royalist management in the early Directory. Preserve the specific phase and avoid treating subsidies as principled Jacobin conversion.

3ABA/33CF must preserve Mirabeau’s constitutional counsel as distinct from restorationist rejection. 1DB supplies the royal maximum-concession baseline, not proof that Mirabeau’s advice simply reproduced that programme.
B888 can internalize Clichy’s role in organizing the electoral turn, alongside press and Institutes. Preserve disunity, shared short-term electoral purposes and remaining violent alternatives.

621/7593 and 23ECC must retain Varennes intensifying and changing the émigré movement. Later Quiberon and Condé receive only relevant later consequences; the event did not create every form of emigration from nothing.

2E013 should retain the concrete movement from wartime difficulties to 1796 and renewed 1797 diplomacy. The broader Pitt strategy must remain in appropriate coalition, naval/colonial and domestic parents; it cannot all be internalized as Lille negotiation content.

0364/7EDE/2E013 must preserve disagreement over peace contributing to the 1797 executive-legislative crisis. Keep domestic constitutional conflict distinct from the subsequent differing Austrian and British settlements; peace was one fault line, not the sole cause.

4E189 must retain blockade constraining imports and army requisitions diverting produce as aggravating causes alongside poor harvests. Avoid treating military demand as the sole origin of the subsistence crisis.

F4D/381386 must retain Doyle’s comparison of renewed coercive dynamics with 1793, while distinguishing post-Fructidor repression from 1799 emergency measures. Page 340’s retrospective synthesis does not make the episodes identical.

5193/F6ED can internalize paper depreciation crippling fiscal operations. Retain the assignat phase on 323 separately from the later mandate attempt and do not reverse cause merely because fiscal failure also worsened the currency crisis.
621/7593 and 23ECC can retain Varennes accelerating militarization and officer emigration. Preserve the already existing émigré centres and preparations; acceleration is not first creation.

8EB/AB9E can internalize Artois’s collaboration with Calonne in the early committee. Do not spread the collaboration unchanged over every later expedition or every page in the old broad evidence union.

FF3E must retain the bankruptcy as abandonment of the Revolution’s commitment to honour inherited public debt, with real creditor losses and annual budget relief. The evaluative meaning is substantive, not disposable label duplication.

B888/6773 must preserve Orleanism as a distinct constitutional dynastic option, with the regicide-parentage calculation. Louis-Philippe’s exile does not make all Clichy constitutionalists an exile organization.
8B56/612D may preserve pacification agreements preceding renewed invasion efforts, with their fragile terms and distrust. Sequence must not be rewritten as a single inevitable cause of Quiberon.
48B can internalize the coup destroying the constitution before its first real test. Preserve continued legal forms, lost credibility and Doyle’s qualified possibility of accommodation.

7593/DCF7/C479/069F must retain the 1792 intervention’s failure and counterproductive political effects within the later defeat argument. Do not attribute every later failure directly or exclusively to that war phase.
5193 must preserve failed emergency levies aggravating fiscal paralysis and state reliance on depreciated paper. F6ED is a later attempted remedy, not the proper sole parent for the 323 tax failure.
032D can internalize class interpretation informing Babeuf’s communist programme. Preserve doctrine, immediate constitutional demands and uneven popular adherence as distinct levels.

5193 must retain differentiated losses to creditors, wage earners and fixed-income households alongside debtor advantage. Full 402–403 confirms uneven incidence, tight credit and lagging wages; the unresolved group label can retire only with that content explicit.
F4D/29CD can internalize Floréal as a distinct instance of Second Directory electoral authoritarianism. Preserve both arbitrary invalidation and remaining parliamentary opposition.
621/04E7 and 9EBF must retain Varennes prompting alarm and diplomacy culminating in conditional Pillnitz. Avoid implying an unconditional agreed invasion or a declaration caused solely by one event.

612D/9EDD must preserve Quiberon’s traumatic military and political consequences, faulty coordination and exposed divisions. Reject a literal trauma to the abstract historical definition; the mechanism belongs to participating counter-revolutionaries and the broader failure assessment.
